roadmap_title: How to adopt AI (a recommended set of steps)

caution_phrases.Standardising the format is a preconditi:
Start by making the information you receive consistent.
Rather than everything at once, it's best to try it on a single piece of work.
caution_phrases.A human must give final approval. Design:
The final check is always done by a person.
It helps to agree up front how AI's output will be reviewed.
caution_phrases.Involves confidential information and le:
Because personal information and legal judgement are involved, AI only helps prepare materials.
Nothing is sent to an outside service.

governance_note: Note: for work handling personal information, limit which folders can be seen and make sure the final decision is always made by a person. As a rule, AI goes as far as 'a draft' or 'a set of candidates'.
dag_subtitle: The flow from receiving information from the customer, through calculation, to payment. The colours show which work involves personal information and which needs a human decision.

terminology_substitutions._comment: Dictionary for automatically replacing jargon in description / ai_fit_reason / ai_role. Substitution is a literal inline swap, so every value must be a drop-in noun or adjective phrase that reads correctly mid-sentence — not a clause. Capitalised variants are listed because the match is case-sensitive and a term may start a sentence.
terminology_substitutions.Human-in-the-loop: a person makes the final call
